title: The case of the missing workday. Our new Assistant is here to investigate.
summary: The new RescueTime Assistant puts all your data and tools in one central location. Learn how it can help you take back control of your day.
body_markdown:
**Case file** : The Missing Workday


**Date** : Tuesday, November 10, 2026


**Time of disappearance** : Approximately 9 am-5 pm


**Evidence recovered** : 13 browser tabs, six meetings, three unfinished tasks, and a suspicious number of Slack notifications


The day started at 9 am with hot coffee and a reasonable to-do list. By 5 pm, the coffee was gone but nothing was crossed off the list.


We’ve all had a day like this, and for some of us, it happens more frequently than we’d like to admit. You can have the ‘busiest’ day in a month, but still end up with no meaningful work to show for it. Blame the meetings, constant stream of notifications, or even your own inability to focus. But until you see actual data about where your time went, it’s really just speculation.


Let’s talk about what’s stealing your time and how RescueTime can help you get it back.


## The usual suspects: Which one stole your workday?


The 8 hours at your computer didn’t just sprout legs and walk away (or so my mom likes to tell me). *Something* is eating up all that time and causing you to work long into the night. Based on nearly 20 years of data from millions of users, here’s the lineup we’ve come to expect.


**The serial interrupter.**


Notifications, emails, messages, and all the other small interruptions that work together to constantly break your concentration.


**The context switcher.**


That hard-to-escape feeling of always being behind forces you to jump between tasks, projects, and apps all day long. You may be up-to-date, but it’s impossible to stay focused for long.


**The meeting monopolist.**


This culprit is sneaky because it’s often out of your control. A calendar too full means that meaningful work has to squeeze into the gaps.


**The five-minute distraction.**


A ‘quick check’ almost always manages to take longer than you anticipated.


**The busywork bandit.**


There are a lot of busywork tasks that make you feel productive but don’t actually help you progress.


Individually, each culprit is pretty innocuous. Together, they can account for a surprising amount of your workday.


This is where our newly redesigned Assistant comes in. With all of the best RescueTime features condensed into one streamlined hub, the new Assistant makes it easier than ever to see where your time goes and regain control over your focus.


## It’s time to examine the evidence in front of you


Your memory isn’t always the most reliable witness when you’re trying to figure out where your workday disappeared.


**Exhibit A** : I started my RescueTime Timer just a few minutes ago to see how long this part of the article took to write. I took a quick break to talk to my babysitter while my kids are napping. Apparently, that conversation wasn’t as short as I thought, because this is what my timer says now:


I need some help, and I know I’m not the only one. Thankfully, the redesigned Assistant puts your time-tracking data, productivity, and insights together in a central location.


Check out how the new Assistant looks compared to the old version:


​


It’s sleeker and more compact, but all your important insights are in one place. Here’s what I love most about it.


### Daily insights


Open the new assistant and you can *almost* hear Emeril shout **BAM!**


All the facts about the way you spent your day are *right there* on your home screen. Before you start customizing, your home includes all of this:


​


​


Of course, you can change your home feed by reorganizing the sections or toggling off what you don’t want to see.


Each section is packed with insights about how you spent your time. At a glance, you can determine which goals you’re still working toward, how much time you’ve spent focused vs. distracted, which tools saw most of your time, what apps were most distracting, and more.


The Assistant is pretty streamlined, so while you only see a couple of items at a time, it takes just a quick scroll to move through all your data.


### Daily feed


Think of the Feed on the new Assistant like you would your Facebook notifications. It keeps you up-to-date about relevant reports and data you might want to check out. You can find it at the very top of your Assistant:​


​


Your Feed changes throughout the day. For example, in the morning, my Feed helps me start the day strong and suggests when I might need help staying focused.


​


​


At the end of my designated work hours, my Feed lets me know my daily report is ready. It’s ready and waiting the next morning if I want to look more closely at where my time went.


## Identify the culprit: Who’s stealing your time?


Looking at a snapshot of your activity data is useful, but recurring patterns can be more revealing about your overall behavior and habits. There are a few different comprehensive reports in the new Assistant.


### Productivity Pulse


A Productivity Pulse is a score based on how you spend your time across different productivity categories. Instead of digging through 18 different data points, it gives you a broader picture of your day.


Your[Pulse](https://help.rescuetime.com/article/61-the-productivity-report) is a time-weighted average of your activities across the five productivity levels. In the new RescueTime assistant, you can see how your productivity is ranking throughout the week and compare that to last week’s data:


​


For a deeper look at how all of your activity impacts your Productivity Pulse, you can still access reports on your web-based[Dashboard](https://www.rescuetime.com/dashboard) .


### Patterns


We all have habits we’re aware of and others that happen so automatically we barely notice them. It’s why some people constantly lose at poker. They don’t even realize they have a tell that’s a dead giveaway.


The Pattern of Your Focus helps you take a closer look at recurring behaviors in the way you work. The Assistant points out your most productive days over the past month:


​


Use this data to plan which days you schedule deep work sessions, or pencil in meetings when you know your focus usually isn’t as strong.


## Prevent the next disappearance


Looking back helps you know how to look forward. The new Assistant can help you take that behavioral data and turn it into action.


### Protect your focus time


I wouldn’t call Focus Sessions one of our best-kept secrets. We consistently rave about their impact, like[this post about teamwide Focus Sessions](https://blog.rescuetime.com/focus-sessions-transform-your-work-culture/) and[this article describing a shared Focus Session](https://blog.rescuetime.com/change-the-way-you-work-with-guided-focus-sessions/) .


However, I *would* say that Focus Sessions are wildly underutilized, given the power they have to keep you on task for an extended period of time. With the new Assistant, it takes just three clicks to start a Focus Session and block out distractions. (Really, I tested it.)


During Focus Sessions, website blocking reduces the temptation to visit distracting websites or respond instantly to Teams messages.


My favorite fun feature is that you can easily turn on music and choose a playlist to accompany your session. It’s another small way to enhance your experience and keep you off distracting apps while you work. ​


### Set goals based on what matters to you


Goals help you monitor the activities and habits you want to prioritize. There are two types of goals you can set: Focus or Timesheets.


Focus goals track how much time you spend on an activity, category, productivity level, or working toward a specific target. You can also turn on automations to fire when you’re at risk of missing your goal or once you reach your target.​


As a freelancer, I especially love how Goals can also be created for Timesheets:


I can set a goal to spend at least an hour working on content for my client who operates on an hourly contract, or set a cap for my hours if I know I shouldn’t exceed a certain number each week.


### Let Automations handle the routine


Productivity becomes a lot easier when you don’t have to constantly force yourself back on track, and you can create an environment that does it for you.


Once you set up Automations, they kick in whenever you meet the established requirements. For example, you can automate RescueTime to block websites for the first 30 minutes of each workday, or set the app to nudge you into your shutdown routine after an eight-hour workday.


We talk more about how to set up automations[in this article](https://help.rescuetime.com/article/459-using-alerts) . Here are just a few ways you can use them:


- Set a hard distraction limit
- Remind yourself to close your inbox after spending too much time on email
- Celebrate reaching your Focus Work goal
- Encourage yourself to stop working on the weekend after an hour or two on your computer


### Account for the work that happens away from your screen


When you’re working on your budget, you still want to account for the money you spend as cash, even though it doesn’t leave a digital trail.


The same is true for the time you spend working offline. It still counts as work; it just didn’t happen on a screen. The new Assistant makes it easy to log those hours and view them within the structure of your entire day. You just select the pen icon next to home and record any relevant information for the time block. Choose one of the three default activities, or click Add Activity + to create custom buttons:


### Dedicate a defined block of time to a task


Focus Sessions work on a countdown basis, but sometimes you want to count *up* instead. A timer is pinned to the top of the new Assistant. You can make a note about what you’re working on, or simply start the timer to see how long a specific task takes you.


## Case closed


Solving the case of the missing workday doesn’t mean you’ll never lose another afternoon to meetings or a distracting email thread. But with the new RescueTime Assistant, you’ll at least have a better idea of where that time goes and which habits send you off track.


When you download the new Assistant, all of your data, settings, and history carry over so you can pick up right where you left off. You can[access it here](https://www.rescuetime.com/get_rescuetime) if you haven’t already made the switch. Happy focusing!
